APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF NOVEMBER 17, 2020

MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY

TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.10.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:07 p.m. Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from
  Closed Session at approximately 7:12 pm.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
  respect to Items 4.1 through 4.10 with the exception of Item 4.8 which was pulled.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of November 17, 2020

meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
consideration at a future meeting.

All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Councilmember Martinez Muela – Upon posting of tonight’s agenda this past Saturday
night the policies of the current administration were on display address highly
controversial and lucrative items with the outgoing lame duck Council. This was true two
years ago when during the final meetings of that Council lucrative contracts were given
and the current Council was forced to deal with the consequences. Then Assistant City
Manager Martinez was given a raise, Police Chief David Reynoso received a raise, and
trash hauler Valley Vista Services was given the last remaining portion of the City
contract without going to RFP for ten years until 2029. The timing and the push through
at that last minute was suspect. On tonight’s agenda in my opinion several of the items
on this agenda are highly suspect in their timing and in their intention. Whether you were
elected 2 weeks ago or 11 years ago to serve the City of El Monte you swore an oath an
oath to protect our City and to defend our Constitution. Are you protecting our City by
allowing more cannabis licenses? Will you consider Baldwin Park’s predicament with
regard to cannabis? Will you consider raising the bar to which these applicants must
comply with prior to licensing? Are you listening to your community who has fought the
capacity of KB Homes from its inception? Even during this pandemic they have
persisted. Will you listen to your own Planning Commission who have denied the project
on unanimous decision 5-0 vote. A re you being fair to one employee by considering an
increase in lifetime benefits while having denied another long time dedicated service and
while our employees are taking furlough days and given this increase while we are still in
the midst of this pandemic. Last question, what will your legacy be? All these questions
will be answered tonight and I hope and pray for the good of the community that you
make decisions on their behalf.

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of November 17, 2020

Selena Solano – I am very proud to have the first female City Manager in the City of El
Monte. We hope that she continues to work on behalf of our families my family has
benefited much by the programming that the City has offered this year. This help has
been indispensable and some of those streets have been fixed and are like new. Very
happy for the work that has been done for her family.

Manuela Saldaña – Very proud to have Alma Martinez as the City Manager and keep
her work on behalf of the City and the families.

Jaqueline Saldaña – I am writing this evening as a lifelong resident of the City of El
Monte and as the current Board President for the Mountain View School District. I want
to take this opportunity to congratulate everyone on a challenging but successful
campaign season. Thank you to everyone who took the initiative to try and represent
this great City. It’s not an easy experience, and so I thank you for your efforts. I look
forward to collaborating with our new Mayor and City Council to serve the best interest
of all of our families. In the spirit of gratefulness, with Thanksgiving around the corner, I
want to thank our current Mayor, City Council Members, and our City Manager for all
that you have done to serve the residents of El Monte. In particular, those families
residing within the boundaries of the Mountain View School District. Thank you to those
of you who, when schools closed, quickly contacted our District to let us know you were
there for our families and asked, “How can we help?” Thank you, Alma Martinez, for
assisting us in obtaining hotspots for our families, who would not have been able to
connect their children for distance learning without them. Thank you for helping to bring
a food pantry to our side of town so that more of our families would have access to food
to feed their families during these trying times. We are a district where over 96 percent
of our students qualify for free and reduced meals, parents are essential workers, and
multiple families live and rent one household. We thank you for the moratorium passed
during this time, allowing many families to maintain their shelter. COVID-19 has hit
them hard. With the collaborative effort of our District and our City, we have met some
of their needs. Thank you to every Department and individual in the City that helped
bring: COVID-19 testing sites; mask and emergency kit giveaways; Hot meals;
After-school activities; Upgraded City Streets; the Halloween celebration; The
Farmer’s Market and other family activities on Main; Fletcher Fetch Park; Mariposa
Skate Park; The upcoming Turkey Give-Away. Thank you for Movies on Main. Mayor
Quintero and City Manager Alma Martinez, you went above and beyond, dressing up to
provide child-friendly and fun reminders and adding some humor and relief for children
and families who have experienced a lot of fear. These acts and events and others not
mentioned show the effectiveness and commitment of our City representatives and our
City Manager to its residents. Thank you to those who our District.

Ron Williams – This meeting violates GC 54950 it is not lawful and we legally recalled
Andre already via petition last year which neither City Hall nor L.A. County Norwalk
could return those signatures for verification.

Catherine – Quintero and Velasco embezzled $10 million from El Monte Promise
Foundation. Velasco committed felony drunk driving and workers compensation
insurance fraud. They need to go to prison Maria Morales don’t screw us again.

Sandra Burdette – El Monte doesn’t need or want marijuana dispensaries. Please
protect our community.

Anonymous – In support of the project.

Mary Ann Powers – The planning commission listened to the residents and denied this project.
103 townhomes will mean at the very least another 206 vehicles traveling the neighborhood on
a daily basis. That added to the traffic brought in by the church is more than that neighborhood,
or for that matter any neighborhood can handle. Let’s respect our residents and deny this
project.

Charles Castaneda – Community activists and spokesperson for neighborhood, does not want
the project. The project does not fit into the existing neighborhood, there are health and traffic
concerns. Traffic is threatening to kids. The Planning Commission voted 5-0 against the project,
and requests the Mayor and Council Members vote no against the project.
Josie Zapata – Against the housing development that residents did not want and knowing that

Irma Zamorano – I would like these projects to be taken out of tonight’s agenda so that the

financial burden to the taxpayers.

Evelyn Beltran Gonzalez – This is a bad idea since there are so many cars already. There is a
lot of traffic already the roads are so narrow and to try and put that big complex with more cars I
don’t see how that is going to work. There is one way in and one way out and it is ridiculous as it
is. I don’t know what everyone is thinking. I don’t see how this is going to work even when they
have their own parking spots and parking garages. Where are all of these cars going to fit.
Howard Owens – I know how crowded that neighborhood is on Sundays the Church. The
Planning Commission has said no to it. I don’t know if the Council has personally driven the
neighborhood to see how narrow the streets are how it is in the morning and in the evening. We
know that environmental reports aren’t every precise sometimes and for a project like that in
that neighborhood with the amount of cars they say 200 and some cars but you know it will be
more like 300 or 400 cars. There is really not enough parking. Put yourself in the residents, I
talked to residents about it and that project doesn’t fit in that neighborhood.

Ms. Medina – A lot of this I don’t understand. I don’t know there are a lot of people who live

Gabriel Ramirez – I am against this project. During these difficult times this project should be
